key_insight: BenchX shows that tumor-detection AI can look strong on average yet fail in specific subgroups defined by patient demographics, tumor characteristics, and scan protocols.
clinical_relevance: The benchmark highlights the need to test medical AI more rigorously across diverse patients and imaging settings before using it in practice.
method: Built an open benchmark from 85,355 CT scans.
Evaluated 12 tumor-detection models across tumor size, location, demographics, and imaging protocol.
Used LLMs to extract and organize subgroup information from clinical data.
evidence_signal: Across large-scale subgroup analysis, state-of-the-art models performed poorly in rare or underrepresented groups, including young, female African Americans.
watch_item: Subgroup findings depend on the quality of clinical-data extraction and may still be limited by sparse labels in rare populations.
paper_title: BenchX: Benchmarking AI Models for Cancer Detection and Localization with Demographic and Protocol Biases
